newsitem.title: USA: U.S. study shows nasal flu vaccine effective.
newsitem.headline: U.S. study shows nasal flu vaccine effective.

text.p: A nasal spray flu vaccine developed by biopharmaceutical company Aviron is very effective at preventing the condition in young children, the government said on Monday.

Only one percent of 1,070 children who received the vaccine in a trial last year developed confirmed influenza, versus 18 percent of children who received a placebo, the National Institutes of Health said.
"The initial results from this trial are very exciting," said Anthony Fauci, director of the NIH's National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID).

"An influenza vaccine given in a nasal spray would be easier to administer and more acceptable than an injection, especially to children. Such a vaccine could have a significant impact on public health," he said.

Aviron will ask the Food and Drug Administration next year to approve use of the vaccine in children and healthy adults, and intends to make it available by prescription for the fall 1999 flu season, NIH said in a statement.
